summary:
Research product recording an explained support mechanism and closing a false lead; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

Investigated and resolved, not escalated: a node whose log is empty but which holds a newer snapshot — the state RecoverCluster deliberately produces by truncating the whole log, and also reachable with TrailingLogs=0 when the FSM has applied through the snapshot index — looked as though it would restart at log index 0, reuse indices below the snapshot, and leave committed client entries unapplied and unanswered (a potential hang). It does not: getLastIndex returns max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex) and getLastEntry returns the snapshot's pair when the snapshot is newer (state.go:157-174), while NewRaft reads the log's last index and restoreSnapshot sets lastApplied and the last snapshot (api.go:631-664). The node advertises and resumes at the snapshot index and dispatchLogs starts from getLastIndex()+1, so no index below the snapshot is reused.

Product contents: new A6 Behavior b-stable-position-reconstruction and Fact f-stable-log-position (with source S54 plus existing S20/S16), so later recovery, compaction or index-reuse questions have a sourced identity for the log/snapshot position instead of re-deriving it. The draft map (base version 9) adds only those two objects and one source; no meaning, identity, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface disposition changed, so the three confirmed findings and every accepted result keep their original basis.

Preserved as open: the ReloadConfig notification-scope lead (only a decreased HeartbeatTimeout signals the notify channels, so a decreased LeaderLeaseTimeout is not picked up until the current lease timer fires); the reachability/consequence premises behind each of the three confirmed findings (unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, heartbeat fast-path election consequence, batching-FSM ConfigurationStore exemption); and the still-unread areas (observer plumbing, file/in-memory snapshot stores, net_transport beyond the heartbeat classification, and the processHeartbeat concurrency contract).
